records.source_title: NSW Government — Nation-leading framework to harness NSW data centre investment
records.verbatim: The NSW Data Centre Policy Framework will make sure future data centre investment is matched with increased investment in renewable energy and water infrastructure. It establishes clear expectations for data centre proponents, with world-class energy, water and environmental standards, meaningful community consultation and appropriate contributions towards the infrastructure needed to support growth.

fields.title: Abolition of the energy-tax reduction for electricity used in data centres (slopad energiskattenedsättning för datorhallar)
fields.status_detail: Decided by the Riksdag 13 December 2022 on the government's 2023 budget bill; changes take effect 1 July 2023.
fields.summary: The Riksdag abolished the energy-tax reduction for electricity used in data centres (datorhallar) from 1 July 2023, on the government's proposal in the 2023 budget bill. The reduction had been introduced in 2017 and was removed after a 2022 National Audit Office report questioned its effect. The change applies to the energy tax on electricity; the refund for electricity used to produce heat or cooling for data centres was also removed in the 2022 Finance Ministry proposal (promemoria, Fi2022/02588, published 9 September 2022).
key_terms: skattenedsättningen för energiskatt på elektrisk kraft som förbrukas i datorhallar slopas

records.source_title: Riksdagen — Näringsutskottets betänkande 2022/23:NU11 (Riksrevisionens rapport om datorhallar)
records.verbatim: Riksdagen beslutade den 13 december 2022 i enlighet med regeringens förslag i budgetpropositionen för 2023 om att skattenedsättningen för energiskatt på elektrisk kraft som förbrukas i datorhallar slopas (prop. 2022/23:1, bet. 2022/23:FiU1, rskr. 2022/23:51). Förändringarna träder i kraft den 1 juli 2023.

translation.text: The Riksdag decided on 13 December 2022, in line with the government's proposal in the 2023 budget bill, to abolish the energy-tax reduction on electricity used in data centres (prop. 2022/23:1, bet. 2022/23:FiU1, rskr. 2022/23:51). The changes take effect on 1 July 2023.

records.notes: Riksdag's own committee report page (data.riksdagen.se, probe HIT on both sentences). The 2022 Finance Ministry promemoria (regeringen.se, Fi2022/02588, 'Publicerad 09 september 2022', probe HIT) is the proposal; it is cited in the summary, not as the status source. The 'Regelrådet' review and the riksdagen skrivelse 2022/23:36 (probe HIT: 'Detta innebär att datorhallar från och med juli 2023 kommer möta samma energiskattemässiga förutsättningar') are supporting. Category 'legislation' is used because the change was made through the budget bill; the statute amendment itself was not read. Principle 'pay_own_way' is an assignment that the change raises data-centre energy-tax costs, not a pledge.

fields.title: Stockholm Data Parks (city-led data-centre heat-recovery initiative)
fields.status_detail: Ongoing city initiative launched 2017 per secondary coverage; the current Stockholm Data Parks site describes it as an initiative.
fields.summary: A City of Stockholm initiative, with Stockholm Exergi, Ellevio and Stokab, that invites data centres to use heat recovery so that waste heat is not wasted and contributes to the city's fossil-free objective. It is a programme, not a binding mandate; the 2017 start date and the Stockholm Exergi heat-purchase arrangement were not verified on a primary page.
key_terms: a data center industry where no heat is wasted

records.source_title: Stockholm Data Parks — Green computing redefined
records.verbatim: Stockholm Data Parks is an initiative by the City of Stockholm, district heating and cooling provider Stockholm Exergi, power grid operator Ellevio and dark fiber provider Stokab. The vision is clear, a data center industry where no heat is wasted. We see data center excess heat as a valuable resource that can be part of fighting climate change.
records.notes: Programme page, not a legal instrument; 'government_framework' follows the spec's use for published non-statutory schemes. Principles left empty: no curator assignment made for this voluntary scheme. Stockholm Exergi's purchase of waste heat in the coldest months, the 2035 10% target and heat-to-apartment figures came from search summaries only and are NOT recorded because the page does not state them. Stockholm Exergi's own page was not read.

fields.title: Data centres moved from electricity tax class II to the general class I from 1 July 2026
fields.status_detail: The Finnish Tax Administration page says electricity used in data centres is moved to class I on 1 July 2026.
fields.summary: Electricity used in data centres (konesalit) moves from the reduced electricity-tax class II to the general class I from 1 July 2026, according to the Finnish Tax Administration. Class II had applied from 2022 to data centres of at least 0.5 MW server power that met energy-use or energy-efficiency criteria. Rates, the revenue estimate and the replacement state-aid scheme were not verified: the government release returned HTTP 403.

translation.text: Electricity used in data centres is moved to tax class I on 1.7.2026.

records.notes: Official tax authority page (probe HIT, final URL after redirect). The law and proposition number (HE 156/2025 vp, per secondary sources) are NOT on the fetched page and are left null. The class II rate (0.05 c/kWh) and class I rate (2.24 c/kWh), and the EUR 47 million revenue estimate, were searched but did not probe-HIT ('2,24' MISS), so they are not recorded. The government release (valtioneuvosto.fi) returned HTTP 403 to probe and WebFetch. The replacement ten-year tax-relief scheme is not recorded. Earlier DCD-sourced 1 January 2026 start date is superseded by the tax authority's 1.7.2026.
